title.en: Volume 107 Book of Later Jin 9: Biographies 4 - Shi Hongzhao, Yang Bin, Wang Zhang, Li Hongjian, Yan Jinqing, Nie Wenjin, Hou Zan, Guo Yuming, Liu Zhu
title.raw: 卷一百〇七 漢書9: 列傳四 史弘肇 楊邠 王章 李洪建 閻晉卿 聶文進 後贊 郭允明 劉銖 Volume 107 Book of Later Jin 9: Biographies 4 - Shi Hongzhao, Yang Bin, Wang Zhang, Li Hongjian, Yan Jinqing, Nie Wenjin, Hou Zan, Guo Yuming, Liu Zhu

sentences.zh: 史宏肇，字化元，鄭州滎澤人也。

translations.literal: Shi Hongzhao, courtesy name Huayuan, was a native of Xingze in Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hongzhao, whose courtesy name was Huayuan, came from Xingze in Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 父潘，本田家。

translations.literal: His father Pan had originally been a farmer.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pan had been a farmer by birth.

sentences.zh: 宏肇少遊俠無行，拳勇健步，日行二百里，走及奔馬。

translations.literal: In youth Hongzhao roamed as a knight-errant without proper conduct; he was bold in boxing, swift of foot, could travel two hundred li in a day, and run as fast as a galloping horse.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man Hongzhao lived as an unruly bravo—fierce with his fists and light on his feet, he could cover two hundred li in a day and keep pace with a galloping horse.

sentences.zh: 梁末，每七戶出一兵，宏肇在籍中，後隸本州開道都，選入禁軍。

translations.literal: At the end of the Liang, one soldier was levied from every seven households; Hongzhao was on the rolls, later came under the Kaidao command of his prefecture, and was selected into the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of the Liang, one man in seven households was drafted for service; Hongzhao was registered, later assigned to his prefecture's Kaidao command, and then chosen for the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 嘗在晉祖麾下，遂留為親從，及踐阼，用為控鶴小校。

translations.literal: He had once served under the Jin ancestor, was kept on as a personal follower, and when the throne was taken was appointed a junior officer of the Crane-Control guard.
translations.idiomatic: He had served under the founding emperor of Jin and was kept on as a personal attendant; when that ruler took the throne, Hongzhao was made a junior officer in the Crane-Control guard.

sentences.zh: 高祖鎮太原，奏請從行，升為牙校，後置武節左右指揮，以宏肇為都將，遙領雷州刺史。

translations.literal: When Gaozu governed Taiyuan, he memorialized asking that Hongzhao accompany him on campaign; he was promoted to a staff captain, and later when the Left and Right Wujie commands were established, Hongzhao was made their chief commander and held the title of prefect of Leizhou in absentia.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu was stationed at Taiyuan, he requested that Hongzhao accompany him and promoted him to a staff captain; later, when the Left and Right Wujie commands were formed, Hongzhao was made their chief commander and given the nominal post of prefect of Leizhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖建號之初，代州王暉叛，以城歸契丹，宏肇征之，一鼓而拔，尋授許州節度使，充侍衛步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Gaozu's founding of the state, Wang Hui of Daizhou rebelled and surrendered the city to the Khitan; Hongzhao campaigned against him, took it at the first assault, and soon received the post of military governor of Xuzhou and served as commander of the palace guard infantry.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Gaozu's reign, Wang Hui of Daizhou rebelled and handed his city over to the Khitan. Hongzhao attacked him and captured the place at the first stroke; he was soon made military governor of Xuzhou and commander of the palace guard infantry.

sentences.zh: 會王守恩以上黨求附，契丹主命大將耿崇美率眾登太行，欲取上黨，高祖命宏肇以軍應援。

translations.literal: It happened that Wang Shou'en sought to submit Shangdang; the Khitan ruler ordered the great general Geng Chongmei to lead troops over the Taihang range intending to seize Shangdang, and Gaozu ordered Hongzhao to march in support.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shou'en offered to surrender Shangdang, the Khitan ruler sent the general Geng Chongmei with an army over the Taihang passes to take the region. Emperor Gaozu ordered Hongzhao to march to its relief.

sentences.zh: 軍至潞州，契丹退去，翟令奇以澤州迎降。

translations.literal: When the army reached Luzhou, the Khitan withdrew, and Zhai Lingqi welcomed them by surrendering Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Luzhou, the Khitan withdrew, and Zhai Lingqi came out to surrender Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 會河陽武行德遣人迎宏肇，遂率眾南下，與行德合。

translations.literal: It happened that Wu Xingde of Heyang sent men to welcome Hongzhao; he then led his troops south and joined Xingde.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xingde of Heyang then sent envoys to welcome Hongzhao, who led his forces south to join him.

sentences.zh: 故高祖由蒲、陜赴洛如歸，宏肇前鋒之功也。

translations.literal: Thus when Gaozu went from Pu and Shaan to Luoyang as if returning home, it was due to Hongzhao's merit as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: It was thanks to Hongzhao's work as vanguard that Emperor Gaozu was able to advance from Pu and Shaan to Luoyang as smoothly as a man coming home.

sentences.zh: 宏肇嚴毅寡言，部轄軍眾，有過無舍，兵士所至，秋毫不犯。

translations.literal: Hongzhao was stern, resolute, and sparing of speech; in commanding troops he showed no leniency for offenses, and wherever his soldiers went they did not take so much as an autumn hair.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao was stern, resolute, and taciturn. He brooked no offense in the troops under his command, and his men would not touch so much as a blade of grass where they passed.

sentences.zh: 部下有指揮使，嘗因指使少不從命，宏肇立撾殺之，將吏股栗，以至平定兩京，無敢幹忤。

translations.literal: Among his subordinates was a commandant who once failed to obey an order over a minor matter of assignment; Hongzhao immediately had him clubbed to death. Officers and clerks trembled in their legs, and through the pacification of the two capitals none dared to cross him.
translations.idiomatic: Once a commandant under him refused a minor assignment; Hongzhao had him beaten to death on the spot. Officers and clerks shook with fear, and through the pacification of the two capitals no one dared defy him.

sentences.zh: 從駕征鄴回，加同平章事，充侍衛親軍都指揮使，兼鎮宋州。

translations.literal: Returning from accompanying the emperor on the campaign against Ye, he was made Tongpingzhangshi, appointed commander of the palace guard personal army, and concurrently governed Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After returning from the emperor's campaign against Ye, he was made a co-equal councilor, appointed commander of the palace guard, and given concurrent command of Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖大漸，與樞密使楊邠、周太祖、蘇逢吉等同受顧命。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was gravely ill, together with the commissioner of military affairs Yang Bin, the Zhou ancestor, and Su Fengji he received the dying charge.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu lay dying, Hongzhao received the emperor's final charge along with Yang Bin, commissioner of military affairs, Guo Wei, and Su Fengji.

sentences.zh: 隱帝嗣位，加檢校太師、兼侍中。

translations.literal: When the Hidden Emperor succeeded, Hongzhao was given the additional titles of honorary grand preceptor and concurrent palace secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yindi came to the throne, Hongzhao was further honored as grand preceptor and made concurrent palace secretary.

sentences.zh: 居無何，河中、永興、鳳翔連橫謀叛，關輔大擾，朝廷日有征發，群情憂揣，亦有不逞之徒，妄構虛語，流布京師。

translations.literal: Before long, Hezhong, Yongxing, and Fengxiang joined in conspiracy to rebel; the Guanfu region was greatly disturbed; the court had daily levies for campaigns; popular feeling was anxious and fearful; and there were also unruly men who falsely fabricated empty talk and spread it through the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Hezhong, Yongxing, and Fengxiang entered into a joint rebellion, throwing the Guanfu region into turmoil. The court issued levy after levy for campaigns, and the people grew anxious; meanwhile unruly elements spread wild rumors through the capital.

sentences.zh: 宏肇都轄禁軍，警衛都邑，專行刑殺，略無顧避，無賴之輩，望風匿跡，路有遺棄，人不敢取。

translations.literal: Hongzhao commanded the palace guard, guarded the capital, and carried out executions exclusively with hardly any scruple; ruffians hid at the sight of him; things abandoned on the road—people did not dare take them.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao commanded the palace guard and policed the capital, meting out executions without scruple. Ruffians hid at his approach, and even goods left in the street went untouched for fear of him.

sentences.zh: 然而不問罪之輕重，理之所在，但雲有犯，便處極刑，枉濫之家，莫敢上訴。

translations.literal: Yet he did not inquire into the lightness or heaviness of guilt or where reason lay; if it was merely said there was an offense, he imposed the extreme penalty. Families wronged and abused did not dare appeal.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he paid no heed to whether a crime was grave or slight or whether justice supported the charge—if anyone was said to have offended, he imposed the death penalty, and families who suffered wrongful punishment did not dare appeal.

sentences.zh: 巡司軍吏，因緣為奸，嫁禍脅人，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Patrol officers and military clerks took advantage of the situation to practice villainy, shifting blame and coercing people—too many to count.
translations.idiomatic: Patrol officers and military clerks used the occasion to practice every kind of villainy, framing the innocent and extorting the helpless—cases beyond numbering.

sentences.zh: （《宋史·邊歸讜傳》：史宏肇怙權專殺，閭裏告訐成風，歸讜言曰：「邇來有匿名書及言風聞事，構害良善，有傷風化，遂使貪吏得以報復私怨，讒夫得以肆其虛誕。

translations.literal: (From the Biography of Bian Guiran in the 《History of Song》: Shi Hongzhao relied on power and killed at will; denunciation in neighborhoods became the fashion. Guiran said: "Recently there have been anonymous letters and reports of hearsay matters that frame and harm the good, injuring public morals, so that greedy officials can repay private grudges and slanderers can give free rein to falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: (From the Biography of Bian Guiran in the 《History of Song》: Shi Hongzhao abused his power and killed at will, until neighborhood denunciation became epidemic. Guiran said, "Of late anonymous letters and hearsay reports have been used to destroy the innocent and corrupt public morals, allowing greedy officials to settle private scores and slanderers to spread their fabrications at will.

sentences.zh: 請明行條制，禁遏誣妄，凡顯有披論，具陳姓名。

translations.literal: I request that regulations be clearly promulgated to forbid and stop false accusations; whenever there is an open accusation, the accuser's name should be fully stated.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that clear regulations be issued to forbid false accusations, and that in every open accusation the accuser's name be recorded in full."

sentences.zh: 其匿名書及風聞事者，並見止絕。

translations.literal: Anonymous letters and hearsay matters should all be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Anonymous letters and hearsay reports should all be prohibited."

sentences.zh: 」論者韙之。）〉

translations.literal: " Commentators approved of this.))〉
translations.idiomatic: Commentators approved of his proposal.))〉

sentences.zh: 時太白晝見，民有仰觀者，為坊正所拘，立斷其腰領。

translations.literal: At the time Venus appeared by day; commoners who looked up to watch were seized by ward heads and immediately had their waists and necks cut through.
translations.idiomatic: When Venus appeared in daylight, any commoner who looked up to watch was seized by the ward head and beheaded on the spot.

sentences.zh: 又有醉民抵忤一軍士，則誣以訛言棄市。

translations.literal: There was also a drunken commoner who offended a soldier; he was falsely charged with seditious talk and executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: A drunken commoner who had brushed against a soldier was falsely accused of spreading sedition and put to death in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 其他斷舌、決口、斫筋、折足者，僅無虛日。

translations.literal: Besides these, those whose tongues were cut out, mouths split, sinews chopped, or feet broken—hardly a day passed without such cases.
translations.idiomatic: Tongues cut out, mouths split open, sinews severed, feet broken—hardly a day passed without such punishments.

sentences.zh: 故相李崧為部曲誣告，族戮於市，取其幼女為婢。

translations.literal: The former chancellor Li Song was falsely denounced by his retainers, his clan was slaughtered in the marketplace, and his young daughter was taken as a maidservant.
translations.idiomatic: The former chancellor Li Song was framed by his own retainers; his entire clan was executed in the marketplace, and his young daughter was taken as a servant girl.

sentences.zh: 自是仕宦之家畜仆隸者，皆以姑息為意，而舊勛故將失勢之後，為廝養輩之所脅制者，往往有之。

translations.literal: From this, official families who kept servants and slaves all took indulgence as their aim, while descendants of old meritorious generals who had lost power were often controlled and coerced by menials.
translations.idiomatic: After this, official households who kept servants learned to indulge them, and it became common for descendants of once-powerful generals to be bullied and controlled by their own menials.

sentences.zh: 軍司孔目吏解暉，性狡而酷，凡有推劾，隨意鍛煉。

translations.literal: The military clerk Xie Hui of the bureau was crafty and cruel by nature; in every investigation he forged evidence as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hui, a military bureau clerk, was by nature cunning and cruel; in every case he investigated he fabricated evidence as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 人有抵軍禁者，被其苦楚，無不自誣以求死所，都人遇之，莫敢仰視。

translations.literal: When people ran afoul of military prohibitions and suffered his torments, none failed to confess falsely in order to find a place to die; when the capital's people met him, none dared look up.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who ran afoul of military law and fell into his hands confessed to whatever he wanted simply to be put out of his misery; people in the capital did not dare even meet his gaze.

sentences.zh: 有燕人何福殷者，以商販為業。

translations.literal: There was a man of Yan named He Fuyin who made his living as a merchant.
translations.idiomatic: There was a man from Yan named He Fuyin who earned his living as a merchant.

sentences.zh: 嘗以十四萬市得玉枕，遣家僮及商人李進賣於淮南，易茗而回。

translations.literal: He once bought a jade pillow for one hundred forty thousand and sent his household slave and the merchant Li Jin to sell it in Huainan, exchanging it for tea before returning.
translations.idiomatic: He once bought a jade pillow for one hundred forty thousand cash and sent his house slave and a merchant named Li Jin to sell it in Huainan, trading it for tea before returning.

sentences.zh: 家僮無行，隱福殷貨財數十萬，福殷責其償，不伏，遂杖之。

translations.literal: The household slave was without proper conduct and concealed several hundred thousand of Fuyin's goods and money; Fuyin demanded repayment, he would not submit, and Fuyin had him beaten.
translations.idiomatic: The house slave was dishonest and embezzled several hundred thousand of Fuyin's money; when Fuyin demanded repayment the slave refused, and Fuyin had him flogged.

sentences.zh: 未幾，家僮詣宏肇上變，言契丹主之入汴也，趙延壽遣福殷賫玉枕陰遺淮南，以致誠意。

translations.literal: Before long the household slave went to Hongzhao to report a treasonous plot, saying that when the Khitan ruler entered Bian, Zhao Yanshou had sent Fuyin bearing the jade pillow to secretly present it to Huainan as a token of sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the slave went to Hongzhao with a denunciation, claiming that when the Khitan ruler entered Bian, Zhao Yanshou had sent Fuyin with the jade pillow as a secret gift to Huainan to win their favor.

sentences.zh: 宏肇即日遣捕福殷等系之。

translations.literal: Hongzhao that same day sent men to arrest Fuyin and the others and imprison them.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao that same day sent men to arrest Fuyin and the others and throw them into prison.

sentences.zh: 解暉希旨，榜掠備至，福殷自誣，連罪者數輩，並棄市。

translations.literal: Xie Hui to please his intent applied flogging to the full; Fuyin confessed falsely, and several persons implicated with him were all executed in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Hui, eager to please, tortured them without mercy until Fuyin confessed; several others implicated in the case were all executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 妻女為宏肇帳下分取之，其家財籍沒。

translations.literal: Wife and daughters were divided up and taken by men under Hongzhao's tent; his household property was registered and confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: His wife and daughters were divided among Hongzhao's retainers, and his property was confiscated to the state.

sentences.zh: 宏肇不喜賓客，嘗言：「文人難耐，輕我輩，謂我輩為卒，可恨可恨！

translations.literal: Hongzhao did not like guests and once said: "Literary men are hard to bear—they look down on people like us and call us soldiers. Hateful, hateful!
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao disliked entertaining guests and once said, "Literary men are unbearable—they look down on men like us and call us common soldiers. Detestable, detestable!

sentences.zh: 」宏肇所領睢陽，其屬府公利，委親吏楊乙就府檢校，貪戾兇橫，負勢生事，吏民畏之，副戎已下，望風展敬。

translations.literal: " Hongzhao governed Suiyang; its subordinate prefectural profits he entrusted to his intimate clerk Yang Yi to inspect at the prefectural office. Greedy, cruel, and violent, Yang relied on power to stir up trouble; clerks and people feared him; from deputy commanders downward all showed respect at his approach.
translations.idiomatic: " Hongzhao governed Suiyang and entrusted its prefectural revenues to his intimate clerk Yang Yi, who inspected the accounts at the prefectural office. Greedy, cruel, and violent, Yang abused his master's power to make trouble; officials and commoners alike feared him, and even deputy commanders bowed low at his approach.

sentences.zh: 聚劍刻剝，無所不至，月率萬緡，以輸宏肇，一境之內，嫉之如仇。

translations.literal: He amassed extortion and exploitation without limit, each month delivering ten thousand strings to Hongzhao; within the whole jurisdiction they hated him as an enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He extorted and exploited without limit, sending ten thousand strings a month to Hongzhao, and throughout the region he was hated as bitterly as a mortal foe.

sentences.zh: （《東都事略·薛居正傳》：史宏肇領侍衛親軍，威震人主，殘忍自恣，人莫敢忤其意。

translations.literal: (From the Biography of Xue Juzheng in the 《Eastern Capital Summary》: Shi Hongzhao commanded the palace guard personal army, his might awed the ruler, he was cruel and willful, and none dared go against his will.
translations.idiomatic: (From the Biography of Xue Juzheng in the 《Eastern Capital Summary》: Shi Hongzhao commanded the palace guard, his power so great it awed the throne itself; cruel and willful, none dared cross him.

sentences.zh: 其部下吏告民犯鹽禁，法當死。

translations.literal: A subordinate clerk of his reported a commoner for violating the salt prohibition, for which the law required death.
translations.idiomatic: One of his subordinate clerks reported a commoner for violating the salt monopoly, a capital offense.

sentences.zh: 居正疑其不實，召詰之，乃其吏以私憾而誣之也。

translations.literal: Juzheng doubted it was true, summoned and questioned him, and it turned out the clerk had falsely accused him out of private resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng doubted the charge, summoned the man, and questioned him; it turned out the clerk had framed him out of private spite.

sentences.zh: 逮捕吏鞫之，具伏，以吏抵法。

translations.literal: He arrested the clerk and interrogated him; he fully confessed, and the clerk was punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Juzheng arrested the clerk, interrogated him until he confessed fully, and had the clerk punished in his place.

sentences.zh: 宏肇雖怒甚，竟亦無以屈也。）〉

translations.literal: Although Hongzhao was very angry, in the end he had no means to bend him.))〉
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao was furious, but in the end he could do nothing to override him.))〉

sentences.zh: 周太祖平河中班師，推功於眾，以宏肇有翊衛鎮重之功，言之於隱帝，即授兼中書令。

translations.literal: When the Zhou ancestor pacified Hezhong and returned the army, he attributed merit to the host and, because Hongzhao had the merit of supporting and guarding the ruler in stabilizing the realm, spoke of this to the Hidden Emperor, who immediately granted him the concurrent title of Zhongshuling.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu of Zhou pacified Hezhong and returned with his army, he gave credit to his commanders and told Emperor Yindi that Hongzhao deserved recognition for guarding the throne and stabilizing the realm; the emperor thereupon made him concurrent Zhongshuling.

sentences.zh: 隱帝自關西賊平之後，昵近小人，太后親族，頗行幹托，宏肇與楊邠甚不平之。

translations.literal: After the Hidden Emperor, since the pacification of the rebels in Guanxi, had grown close to petty men and the empress dowager's kin, who frequently practiced solicitation, Hongzhao and Yang Bin were very displeased.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion in Guanxi was put down, Emperor Yindi grew close to petty favorites and the empress dowager's kin, who frequently used their influence to secure appointments; Hongzhao and Yang Bin were deeply displeased.

sentences.zh: 太后有故人子求補軍職，宏肇怒而斬之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager had an old acquaintance's son seek a military post; Hongzhao in anger beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager's old acquaintance sought a military post for his son, Hongzhao had the young man beheaded in a rage.

sentences.zh: 帝始聽樂，賜教坊使玉帶，諸伶官錦袍，往謝宏肇，宏肇讓之曰：「健兒為國戍邊，忍寒冒暑，未能遍有沾賜，爾輩何功，敢當此賜！

translations.literal: The emperor had begun to listen to music and bestowed a jade belt on the director of the music office and brocade robes on the players; they went to thank Hongzhao, who rebuked them saying: "Stalwart soldiers guard the borders for the state, enduring cold and heat, and cannot all receive such favors—what merit have you to dare accept this gift!
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor began patronizing music and gave the director of the music office a jade belt and brocade robes to the players, they went to thank Hongzhao. He rebuked them: "Our soldiers endure cold and heat on the frontier and cannot all receive such rewards—what have you done to deserve this!

sentences.zh: 」盡取袍帶還官，其兇戾如此。

translations.literal: " He took all the robes and belts back to the office—so violent and overbearing was he.
translations.idiomatic: " He seized the robes and belt and returned them to the palace stores—such was his brutal arrogance.

sentences.zh: 周太祖有鎮鄴之命，宏肇欲兼領機樞之任，蘇逢吉異其議，宏肇忿之。

translations.literal: The Zhou ancestor received the order to govern Ye; Hongzhao wished to hold the military affairs commission concurrently, Su Fengji differed from his view, and Hongzhao resented him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu of Zhou was ordered to govern Ye, Hongzhao wanted to keep the military affairs commission for himself; Su Fengji disagreed, and Hongzhao bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 翌日，因竇貞固飲會，貴臣悉集，宏肇厲色舉爵屬周太祖曰：「昨晨廷論，一何同異！

translations.literal: The next day, at a drinking gathering hosted by Dou Zhengu, all the great ministers assembled; Hongzhao with stern countenance raised his cup and addressed the Zhou ancestor: "Yesterday morning's court discussion—how great the disagreement!
translations.idiomatic: The next day, at a banquet given by Dou Zhengu with all the great ministers present, Hongzhao raised his cup with a dark expression and addressed Guo Wei: "Yesterday's debate in court—what a disagreement that was!

sentences.zh: 今日與弟飲此。

translations.literal: Today let younger brother drink this with me.
translations.idiomatic: Today let us drink this together, younger brother.

sentences.zh: 」楊邠、蘇逢吉亦舉大爵曰：「此國家之事也，何足介意！

translations.literal: " Yang Bin and Su Fengji also raised large cups and said: "This is a matter of state—what is there to mind!
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Bin and Su Fengji also raised their cups and said, "This is a matter of state—why take it to heart!

sentences.zh: 」俱飲釂。

translations.literal: " All drank to the bottom.
translations.idiomatic: " They all drained their cups.

sentences.zh: 宏肇又厲聲言曰：「安朝廷，定禍亂，直須長槍大劍，至如毛錐子，焉足用哉！

translations.literal: Hongzhao again spoke in a harsh voice: "To settle the court and quell disorder, one needs only long spears and great swords—as for brush pens, of what use are they!
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao spoke up again in a harsh voice: "To secure the court and quell disorder you need long spears and great swords—what use are writing brushes!

sentences.zh: 」三司使王章曰：「雖有長槍大劍，若無毛錐子，贍軍財賦，自何而集？

translations.literal: " The commissioner of the three departments Wang Zhang said: "Although there are long spears and great swords, without brush pens, from where would the funds and taxes to supply the army be gathered?
translations.idiomatic: " Wang Zhang, commissioner of the three departments, replied, "You may have long spears and great swords, but without writing brushes, where would the funds and taxes to supply the army come from?

sentences.zh: 」宏肇默然，少頃而罷。

translations.literal: " Hongzhao was silent, and after a little while the gathering broke up.
translations.idiomatic: " Hongzhao fell silent, and after a moment the gathering broke up.

sentences.zh: 未幾，三司使王章於其第張酒樂，時宏肇與宰相、樞密使及內客省使閻晉卿等俱會。

translations.literal: Before long the commissioner of the three departments Wang Zhang spread wine and music at his residence; at the time Hongzhao met together with the chancellors, the commissioner of military affairs, and the commissioner of the inner service Yan Jinqing and others.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Wang Zhang gave a banquet with wine and music at his residence, attended by Hongzhao, the chancellors, the commissioner of military affairs, and Yan Jinqing, commissioner of the inner service, among others.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，為手勢令，宏肇不熟其事，而閻晉卿坐次宏肇，屢教之。

translations.literal: When the wine was warm, they played the hand-gesture game; Hongzhao was not familiar with it, and Yan Jinqing, seated next to Hongzhao, repeatedly instructed him.
translations.idiomatic: As the drinking warmed up they played a hand-gesture drinking game; Hongzhao did not know the rules, and Yan Jinqing, seated beside him, kept coaching him.

sentences.zh: 蘇逢吉戲宏肇曰：「近坐有姓閻人，何憂罰爵！

translations.literal: Su Fengji jested with Hongzhao: "The man seated nearby has the surname Yan—why worry about a penalty cup!
translations.idiomatic: Su Fengji teased Hongzhao: "You have a man surnamed Yan sitting right beside you—why worry about drinking a forfeit!

sentences.zh: 」宏肇妻閻氏，本酒妓也，宏肇謂逢吉譏之，大怒，以醜語詬逢吉。

translations.literal: " Hongzhao's wife was surnamed Yan and had originally been a wine-house entertainer; Hongzhao thought Fengji was mocking him, flew into a rage, and reviled Fengji with foul language.
translations.idiomatic: " Hongzhao's wife was surnamed Yan and had once been a tavern entertainer; Hongzhao thought Fengji was mocking her, flew into a rage, and showered him with foul abuse.

sentences.zh: 逢吉不校，宏肇欲毆逢吉，逢吉策馬而去，宏肇遽起索劍，意欲追逢吉。

translations.literal: Fengji did not contend; Hongzhao wanted to beat Fengji; Fengji spurred his horse and fled; Hongzhao sprang up seeking a sword, intending to pursue Fengji.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji did not answer back, but Hongzhao tried to strike him; Fengji spurred his horse and fled while Hongzhao leaped up for a sword, intent on chasing him down.

sentences.zh: 楊邠曰：「蘇公是宰相，公若害之，致天子何地，公細思之！

translations.literal: Yang Bin said: "Master Su is a chancellor—if you harm him, where will that leave the Son of Heaven? My lord, think carefully!
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bin said, "Master Su is a chancellor—if you kill him, what will become of the emperor? Think carefully!

sentences.zh: 」邠泣下。

translations.literal: " Bin wept.
translations.idiomatic: " Bin wept as he spoke.

sentences.zh: 宏肇索馬急馳而去，邠慮有非常，連鑣而進，送至第而還。

translations.literal: Hongzhao sought a horse and galloped away in haste; Bin feared something extraordinary and urged his horse forward in succession, escorting him to his residence before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao seized a horse and galloped off; Bin, fearing worse trouble, rode after him in haste and escorted him home before returning.

sentences.zh: 自是將相不協如水火矣。

translations.literal: From this the generals and chancellors were as incompatible as fire and water.
translations.idiomatic: From that day the generals and chancellors were as incompatible as fire and water.

sentences.zh: 隱帝遣王峻將酒樂於公子亭以和之，竟不能解。

translations.literal: The Hidden Emperor sent Wang Jun with wine and music to the Prince's Pavilion to reconcile them, but in the end could not resolve it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yindi sent Wang Jun with wine and music to the Prince's Pavilion to reconcile them, but the breach could not be healed.

sentences.zh: 其後李業、郭允明、後贊、聶文進居中用事，不悅執政。

translations.literal: After this Li Ye, Guo Yuming, Hou Zan, and Nie Wenjin held power within the palace and were displeased with those in office.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Li Ye, Guo Yuming, Hou Zan, and Nie Wenjin held sway within the palace and resented the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 又見隱帝年漸長，厭為大臣所制，嘗有忿言，業等乃乘間譖宏肇等，隱帝稍以為信。

translations.literal: They also saw that the Hidden Emperor was gradually growing older, weary of being controlled by great ministers, and had sometimes spoken in anger; Ye and the others then seized the opportunity to slander Hongzhao and the others, and the Hidden Emperor gradually came to believe them.
translations.idiomatic: They also saw that Emperor Yindi was growing older and resented being controlled by his ministers; when he spoke in anger, they seized the chance to slander Hongzhao and the others, and the emperor gradually came to believe them.

sentences.zh: 業等乃言宏肇等專權震主，終必為亂，隱帝益恐。

translations.literal: Ye and the others then said that Hongzhao and the others monopolized power and awed the ruler, and would ultimately bring disorder; the Hidden Emperor grew more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: They told the emperor that Hongzhao and his colleagues monopolized power, overshadowed the throne, and would surely bring rebellion; Emperor Yindi grew more afraid.

sentences.zh: 嘗一夕，聞作坊鍛甲之聲，疑外有兵仗卒至，達旦不寐。

translations.literal: Once one night he heard the sound of armor being forged in the workshop, suspected that troops and weapons outside were about to arrive, and did not sleep until dawn.
translations.idiomatic: One night he heard armor being hammered in the workshops, imagined that troops were about to march on the palace, and lay awake until dawn.

sentences.zh: 自是與業等密謀禁中，欲誅宏肇等。

translations.literal: From this he secretly plotted within the palace with Ye and the others to execute Hongzhao and the others.
translations.idiomatic: From then on he plotted secretly within the palace with Ye and the others to kill Hongzhao and his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 議定，入白太后，太后曰：「此事豈可輕發耶！

translations.literal: When the plan was settled, he entered to inform the empress dowager; the empress dowager said: "How can this matter be lightly launched!
translations.idiomatic: When the plan was set, he went to tell the empress dowager. She said, "How can you launch such a thing lightly!

sentences.zh: 更問宰臣等。

translations.literal: Ask the chancellors and others again.
translations.idiomatic: Consult the chancellors again first."

sentences.zh: 」李業在側，曰：「先皇帝言，朝廷大事，莫共措大商量。

translations.literal: " Li Ye was at his side and said: "The late emperor said that for great affairs of state one must not consult with those fellows.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Ye, standing beside him, said, "The late emperor said that great affairs of state must not be discussed with those fellows.

sentences.zh: 」太后又言之，隱帝怒曰：「閨門之內，焉知國家之事！

translations.literal: " The empress dowager spoke again; the Hidden Emperor said angrily: "Within the women's quarters, how would one know affairs of state!
translations.idiomatic: " The empress dowager spoke again, and Emperor Yindi flared up: "What does the inner quarters know of affairs of state!

sentences.zh: 」拂衣而出。

translations.literal: " He brushed his robes and went out.
translations.idiomatic: " He flung his sleeve and stormed out.

sentences.zh: 內客省使閻晉卿潛知其事，乃詣宏肇私第，將欲告之，宏肇以他事拒之不見。

translations.literal: The commissioner of the inner service Yan Jinqing secretly knew of the matter and went to Hongzhao's private residence intending to inform him, but Hongzhao refused to see him on the pretext of other business.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jinqing, commissioner of the inner service, learned of the plot in secret and went to Hongzhao's house to warn him, but Hongzhao refused to see him, pleading other business.

sentences.zh: 乾祐三年冬十一月十三日，宏肇入朝，與樞密使楊邠、三司使王章同坐於廣政殿東廡下，俄有甲士數十人自內而出，害宏肇等於閣，夷其族。

translations.literal: On the thirteenth day of the eleventh month of winter in the third year of Qianyou, Hongzhao entered court; together with the commissioner of military affairs Yang Bin and the commissioner of the three departments Wang Zhang he sat under the eastern veranda of the Guangzheng Hall; presently several tens of armored soldiers came out from within and killed Hongzhao and the others at the pavilion, exterminating their clans.
translations.idiomatic: On the thirteenth day of the eleventh month of winter in the third year of Qianyou, Hongzhao came to court and sat with Yang Bin and Wang Zhang under the eastern veranda of the Guangzheng Hall. Suddenly several dozen armored soldiers emerged from within the palace, killed Hongzhao and his colleagues in the pavilion, and exterminated their families.

sentences.zh: 先是，宏肇第數有異，嘗一日，於階砌隙中有煙氣蓬勃而出。

translations.literal: Earlier Hongzhao's residence had repeatedly shown omens; once one day from a crack in the steps smoke billowed forth.
translations.idiomatic: Before this Hongzhao's residence had shown several omens; once smoke billowed up from a crack in the stone steps.

sentences.zh: 禍前二日昧爽，有星落於宏肇前三數步，如迸火而散，俄而被誅。

translations.literal: Two days before the disaster at dawn a star fell several paces before Hongzhao, scattering like bursting fire, and soon after he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Two days before his death, at dawn, a star fell a few paces before him and scattered like bursting flame; soon afterward he was killed.

sentences.zh: 周太祖踐阼，追封鄭王，以禮葬，官為立碑。

translations.literal: When the Zhou ancestor took the throne, he posthumously enfeoffed him as Prince of Zheng, buried him with ceremony, and had officials erect a stele.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu of Zhou took the throne, he posthumously enfeoffed Hongzhao as Prince of Zheng, buried him with full honors, and had a stele erected at his tomb.

sentences.zh: 宏肇子德充，乾祐中，授檢校司空，領忠州刺史。

translations.literal: Hongzhao's son Dechong, during Qianyou, was appointed honorary Sikong and governed Zhongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhao's son Dechong, during the Qianyou reign, was made honorary Sikong and given Zhongzhou as his prefecture.

sentences.zh: 粗讀書，親儒者，常不悅父之所為。

translations.literal: He had a rough knowledge of books, was close to Confucian scholars, and was often displeased with his father's conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He had some schooling, cultivated the company of scholars, and was often ashamed of his father's conduct.

sentences.zh: 貢院嘗錄一學科於省門叫噪，申中書門下，宰相蘇逢吉令送侍衛司，請痛笞刺面。

translations.literal: Once at the examination compound a cohort of candidates raised an uproar at the provincial gate; the matter was reported to the Secretariat-Chancellery, and the chancellor Su Fengji ordered them sent to the palace guard office with a request for severe flogging and facial branding.
translations.idiomatic: Once a group of examination candidates raised a disturbance at the provincial gate; the matter was reported to the Secretariat, and Chancellor Su Fengji ordered them sent to the palace guard for severe flogging and facial branding.

sentences.zh: 德充聞之，白父曰：「書生無禮，有府縣御史臺，非軍務治也。

translations.literal: When Dechong heard of it, he told his father: "Scholars were without propriety—there are the prefecture, county, and censorate to handle this; it is not a matter for military administration.
translations.idiomatic: When Dechong heard of this, he told his father, "These were unruly scholars—there are prefectural offices and the censorate to deal with them; this is not a matter for the military.

sentences.zh: 公卿如此，蓋欲彰大人之過。

translations.literal: For the high ministers to act thus would only serve to display the great man's faults.
translations.idiomatic: If the high ministers act this way, they only make your faults more visible."

sentences.zh: 」宏肇深以為然，即破械放之。

translations.literal: " Hongzhao deeply thought it right and immediately broke their shackles and released them.
translations.idiomatic: " Hongzhao saw the force of this and at once had their shackles removed and set them free.

sentences.zh: 後之識者尤嘉德充之為人焉。

translations.literal: Later men of judgment especially praised Dechong's character.
translations.idiomatic: Later commentators especially praised Dechong's character.

sentences.zh: 楊邠，魏州冠氏人也。

translations.literal: Yang Bin was a native of Guanshi in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Bin came from Guanshi in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 少以吏給事使府，後唐租庸使孔謙，即其妻之世父也。

translations.literal: In youth he served as a clerk in the commissionerer's office; Kong Qian, grain-and-corvée commissioner of Later Tang, was his wife's father's cousin.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he served as a clerk in a commissionerer's office; Kong Qian, Later Tang's grain-and-corvée commissioner, was his wife's uncle.

sentences.zh: 謙領度支，補勾押官，歷孟、華、鄆三州糧料使。

translations.literal: When Qian headed the revenue bureau, Bin was appointed a checking and custody clerk and served successively as grain commissioner of Meng, Hua, and Yan prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian headed the revenue bureau, Bin was appointed a checking clerk and served in turn as grain commissioner for Meng, Hua, and Yan prefectures.

sentences.zh: 高祖為鄴都留守，用為左都押衙，高祖鎮太原，益加親委。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was military governor of Yedu, he employed Bin as left chief military adjutant; when Gaozu governed Taiyuan, he entrusted him still more closely.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu was military governor of Yedu, he made Bin his left chief military adjutant; when Gaozu took up his post at Taiyuan, he relied on him even more closely.

sentences.zh: 漢國建，遷檢校太保、權樞密使。

translations.literal: When the Han state was founded, he was transferred to honorary grand guardian and acting commissioner of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han state was founded, he was made honorary grand guardian and acting commissioner of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 汴、洛平，正拜樞密使、檢校太傅。

translations.literal: When Bian and Luoyang were pacified, he was formally appointed commissioner of military affairs and honorary grand mentor.
translations.idiomatic: After Bian and Luoyang were pacified, he was formally appointed commissioner of military affairs and honorary grand mentor.

sentences.zh: 及高祖大漸，與蘇逢吉、史宏肇等同受顧命，輔立嗣君。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was gravely ill, together with Su Fengji, Shi Hongzhao, and the others he received the dying charge and assisted in establishing the heir.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu lay dying, he received the final charge along with Su Fengji, Shi Hongzhao, and the others, and helped install the heir to the throne.

sentences.zh: 隱帝即位，宰臣李濤上章，請出邠與周太祖為藩鎮，邠等泣訴於太后，由是罷濤而相邠，加中書侍郎兼吏部尚書、同平章事，仍兼樞密使。

translations.literal: When the Hidden Emperor took the throne, the chief minister Li Tao memorialized asking that Bin and the Zhou ancestor be sent out as military governors of border regions; Bin and the others wept and pleaded before the empress dowager; thereby Tao was dismissed and Bin made chancellor, with the added titles of vice director of the Secretariat and concurrent minister of personnel and Tongpingzhangshi, still holding the military affairs commission concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yindi came to the throne, Chancellor Li Tao memorialized asking that Yang Bin and Guo Wei be sent out to govern border regions as military governors. Bin and his allies wept before the empress dowager; Tao was dismissed, Bin was made chancellor with the titles of vice director of the Secretariat, minister of personnel, and Tongpingzhangshi, and he retained the military affairs commission.

sentences.zh: 時中書除吏太多，訛謬者眾。

translations.literal: At the time the Secretariat appointed too many officials, and errors were numerous.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Secretariat was appointing too many officials, and mistakes were common.

sentences.zh: 及邠居相位，帝一以委之，凡南衙奏事，中書除命，先委邠斟酌，如不出邠意，至於一簿一掾，亦不聽從。

translations.literal: When Bin held the chancellorship, the emperor entrusted everything to him; all matters reported from the southern offices and all Secretariat appointments were first referred to Bin for deliberation; if they did not accord with Bin's intent, even a single register or clerk was not approved.
translations.idiomatic: Once Bin held the chancellorship, the emperor entrusted everything to him. Every report from the southern offices and every Secretariat appointment passed through Bin first; if it did not suit him, not even the smallest clerkship was approved.

sentences.zh: 邠雖長於吏事，不識大體，常言：「為國家者，但得帑藏豐盈，甲兵強盛，至於文章禮樂，並是虛事，何足介意也。

translations.literal: Although Bin was skilled in clerical affairs, he did not grasp the larger pattern and often said: "For the state, one need only have the treasury full and armor and troops strong; as for literature, rites, and music, these are all empty matters—what is there to mind?
translations.idiomatic: Bin was skilled in administration but lacked breadth of vision. He often said, "To govern a state you need only a full treasury and strong armies; literature, rites, and music are empty things—why bother with them?

sentences.zh: 」平河中，邠加右僕射。

translations.literal: " When Hezhong was pacified, Bin was made right vice director of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: " After Hezhong was pacified, Bin was made right vice director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 邠既專國政，觸事苛細，條理煩碎。

translations.literal: Once Bin monopolized state affairs, he was harsh and minute in every matter, with regulations tedious and fragmented.
translations.idiomatic: Once Bin controlled the government, he was harsh and petty in every matter, piling regulation upon regulation.

sentences.zh: 前資官不得於外方居止，自京師至諸州府，行人往來，並須給公憑。

translations.literal: Former officials were not permitted to reside outside the capital; from the capital to all prefectures and districts, travelers coming and going all had to be issued official passes.
translations.idiomatic: Former officials were forbidden to live outside the capital, and from the capital to every prefecture travelers had to carry official passes.

sentences.zh: 所由司求請公憑者，朝夕填咽，旬日之間，民情大擾，行路擁塞，邠乃止其事。

translations.literal: The responsible offices seeking and issuing official passes were jammed morning and evening; within ten days popular feeling was greatly disturbed and the roads congested, and Bin then stopped the measure.
translations.idiomatic: The offices that issued the passes were overwhelmed day and night; within ten days the people were in an uproar and the roads jammed, and Bin abandoned the policy.

sentences.zh: 時史宏肇恣行慘酷，殺戮日眾，都人士庶，相目於路，邠但稱宏肇之善。

translations.literal: At the time Shi Hongzhao practiced cruelty at will and killings daily multiplied; gentlemen and commoners of the capital exchanged glances on the road, yet Bin only praised Hongzhao's merits.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hongzhao was killing freely and the executions multiplied daily; people in the capital exchanged fearful glances in the streets, yet Bin spoke only of Hongzhao's virtues.

sentences.zh: 太后弟武德使李業求為宣徽使，隱帝與太后重違之，私訪於邠，邠以朝廷內使，遷拜有序，不可超居，遂止。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's younger brother, Military Virtue Commissioner Li Ye, sought the post of commissioner of the palace secretariat; the Hidden Emperor and empress dowager were deeply reluctant to refuse, and privately consulted Bin, who said that inner-service posts of the court had an orderly sequence of promotion and could not be skipped, and so it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager's brother Li Ye, Military Virtue Commissioner, sought the post of palace secretariat commissioner. Emperor Yindi and the empress dowager were reluctant to refuse and consulted Bin privately; Bin said inner-service posts had a fixed order of promotion and could not be skipped, and the appointment was blocked.

sentences.zh: 隱帝所愛耿夫人，欲立為後，邠亦以為太速。

translations.literal: The Hidden Emperor's beloved Lady Geng he wished to make empress; Bin also thought it too soon.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to make his beloved Lady Geng empress; Bin thought it premature.

sentences.zh: 夫人卒，隱帝欲以後禮葬，邠又止之，隱帝意不悅，左右有承間進甘言者，隱帝益怒之。

translations.literal: When the lady died, the Hidden Emperor wished to bury her with empress rites; Bin again stopped it; the Hidden Emperor was displeased; attendants who seized the opportunity offered sweet words, and the Hidden Emperor grew angrier at him.
translations.idiomatic: When she died the emperor wished to bury her with empress honors; Bin again objected. The emperor was displeased, and when flatterers seized the chance to whisper in his ear, his anger at Bin only grew.

sentences.zh: （案：此下疑有闕文。）〉

translations.literal: (Note: Text below this point is suspected to be missing.))〉
translations.idiomatic: (Note: Text below this point is believed missing.))〉

sentences.zh: 邠繕甲兵，實帑廩，俾國用不闕，邊鄙粗寧，亦其功也。

translations.literal: Bin repaired armor and weapons and filled the granaries, so that state expenditures were not lacking and the border regions were roughly at peace—this too was his merit.
translations.idiomatic: Bin repaired arms and filled the granaries, kept state finances solvent, and brought rough peace to the borders—these were his merits as well.

sentences.zh: （《宣和書譜》云：邠末年留意縉紳，延客門下，知經史有用，乃課吏傳寫。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Catalogue of Xuanhe Calligraphy》 says: In his later years Bin turned his attention to the gentry, kept guests at his gate, recognized the usefulness of the classics and histories, and set clerks to copying them.))〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Catalogue of Xuanhe Calligraphy》 says: In his later years Bin cultivated the company of scholars, kept guests at his door, recognized the value of the classics and histories, and set his clerks to copying them.))〉

sentences.zh: 王章，大名南樂人也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhang was a native of Nanle in Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhang came from Nanle in Daming.

sentences.zh: 少為吏，給事使府。

translations.literal: In youth he was a clerk serving in a commissionerer's office.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he served as a clerk in a commissionerer's office.

sentences.zh: 同光初，隸樞密院，後歸本郡，累職至都孔目官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he was attached to the Bureau of Military Affairs; later he returned to his home commandery and rose through posts to chief registry clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tongguang reign he served in the Bureau of Military Affairs; later he returned home and rose to chief registry clerk.

sentences.zh: 後唐清泰末，屯駐捧聖都虞候張令昭作亂，逐節度使劉延皓，自稱留後，章以本職為令昭役使。

translations.literal: At the end of Qingtai in Later Tang, Zhang Lingzhao, stationed assistant commander of the Sacred Guard, rebelled, drove out the military governor Liu Yanhao, and styled himself acting governor; Zhang served Lingzhao in his original post.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Qingtai reign in Later Tang, Zhang Lingzhao, assistant commander of the Sacred Guard garrison, rebelled, expelled Military Governor Liu Yanhao, and declared himself acting governor; Wang Zhang served him in his former capacity.

sentences.zh: 末帝遣範延光討平之，搜索叛黨甚急。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor sent Fan Yanguang to suppress him; the search for rebel associates was very urgent.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor sent Fan Yanguang to put down the rebellion and hunted rebel associates relentlessly.

sentences.zh: 章之妻即白文珂之女也，文珂與副招討李敬周善，以章為托。

translations.literal: Zhang's wife was the daughter of Bai Wenke; Wenke was on good terms with the deputy pacification commissioner Li Jingzhou and entrusted Zhang to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhang's wife was the daughter of Bai Wenke, who was friendly with Deputy Pacification Commissioner Li Jingzhou and asked him to protect Zhang.

sentences.zh: 及攻下逆城，敬周匿之，載於橐駝褚中，竄至洛下，匿於敬周之私第。

translations.literal: When the rebel city was taken, Jingzhou hid him, loaded him in a camel bag, fled to Luoyang, and concealed him in Jingzhou's private residence.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel city fell, Jingzhou hid him in a camel-load bag, smuggled him to Luoyang, and concealed him in his private house.

sentences.zh: 及末帝敗，章為省職，歷沔陽糧料使。

translations.literal: When the Last Emperor was defeated, Zhang held a provincial post and served as grain commissioner of Mianyang.
translations.idiomatic: After the Last Emperor's defeat, Zhang held a provincial post and served as grain commissioner of Mianyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖典侍衛親軍，詔為都孔目官，從至河東，專委錢谷。

translations.literal: When Gaozu commanded the palace guard personal army, he was ordered to be chief registry clerk, accompanied him to Hedong, and was entrusted exclusively with funds and grain.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu commanded the palace guard, Zhang was made chief registry clerk, accompanied him to Hedong, and was put in charge of finances and supplies.

sentences.zh: 國初，授三司使、檢校太傅，從征杜重威於鄴下。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state he was appointed commissioner of the three departments and honorary grand mentor, and accompanied the campaign against Du Chongwei at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the dynasty he was made commissioner of the three departments and honorary grand mentor, and joined the campaign against Du Chongwei at Ye.

sentences.zh: 明年，高祖崩，隱帝即位，加檢校太尉、同平章事。

translations.literal: The next year Gaozu died and the Hidden Emperor succeeded; Zhang was given the additional titles of honorary grand marshal and Tongpingzhangshi.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Emperor Gaozu died and Emperor Yindi succeeded; Zhang was made honorary grand marshal and Tongpingzhangshi.

sentences.zh: 居無何，蒲、雍、岐三鎮畔。

translations.literal: Before long the three regions of Pu, Yong, and Qi rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Pu, Yong, and Qi rebelled.

sentences.zh: 是時，契丹犯闕之後，國家新造，物力未充。

translations.literal: At this time, after the Khitan violation of the capital, the state was newly founded and material resources were not yet sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan had lately sacked the capital, the dynasty was newly founded, and resources were scarce.

sentences.zh: 章與周太祖、史宏肇、楊邠等盡心王室，知無不為，罷不急之務，惜無用之費，收聚財賦，專事西征，軍旅所資，供饋無乏。

translations.literal: Zhang, together with the Zhou ancestor, Shi Hongzhao, Yang Bin, and others devoted themselves to the royal house, doing all they knew; they suspended non-urgent affairs, spared useless expenditures, gathered taxes and levies, and devoted themselves to the western campaign; what the army needed in supplies was never lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, together with Guo Wei, Shi Hongzhao, Yang Bin, and others, devoted themselves wholly to the throne, cutting nonessential spending, gathering revenue, and focusing on the western campaign; the army was never short of supplies.

sentences.zh: 及三叛平，賜與之外，國有餘積。

translations.literal: When the three rebellions were pacified, beyond rewards and gifts the state had surplus accumulations.
translations.idiomatic: When the three rebellions were put down, the state had surplus funds beyond rewards and gifts.

sentences.zh: 然以專於權利，剝下過當，斂怨歸上，物論非之。

translations.literal: Yet because he was devoted to power and profit and stripped the people excessively, resentment was gathered upon the ruler, and public opinion condemned him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because he was obsessed with power and profit and squeezed the people too hard, popular resentment fell on the throne, and public opinion condemned him.

sentences.zh: 舊制，秋夏苗租，民稅一斛，別輸二升，謂之「雀鼠耗」。

translations.literal: By old regulation, for autumn and summer field rents, for each hu of tax paid by the people an additional two sheng was delivered, called "sparrow-and-rat loss."
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, for autumn and summer field rents the people paid an extra two sheng per hu of tax, called the "sparrow-and-rat allowance."

sentences.zh: 乾祐中，輸一斛者，別令輸二斗，目之為「省耗」。

translations.literal: During Qianyou, for each hu delivered an additional two dou was required, termed "provincial loss."
translations.idiomatic: During Qianyou, for each hu delivered the people had to pay an additional two dou, called the "provincial allowance."

sentences.zh: 百姓苦之。

translations.literal: The common people suffered from it.
translations.idiomatic: The people suffered bitterly under this.

sentences.zh: 又，官庫出納緡錢，皆以八十為陌，至是民輸者如舊，官給者以七十七為陌，遂為常式。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the official treasury's receipt and disbursement of strings of cash, eighty per hundred was the standard; now the people paid as before but official payments used seventy-seven per hundred, and this became the regular practice.
translations.idiomatic: Official cash had long been counted at eighty per hundred; now the people still paid at eighty, but the government paid out at seventy-seven, and this became permanent practice.

sentences.zh: （《歸田錄》：用錢之法，自五代以來，以七十七為百，謂之「省陌」。

translations.literal: (The 《Record of Retirement》: The method of using money, since the Five Dynasties, has taken seventy-seven as one hundred, called "provincial per-hundred."
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Record of Retirement》: Since the Five Dynasties, money has been counted at seventy-seven to the hundred, called "provincial per-hundred."

sentences.zh: 今市井交易，又克其五，謂之「依除」。）〉

translations.literal: Today in market transactions they deduct five more, called "deduction by rule."))〉
translations.idiomatic: In market trade today five more are deducted, called "rule-based deduction."))〉

sentences.zh: 民有訴田者，雖無十數戶，章必命全州覆視，幸其廣有苗額，以增邦賦，曾未數年，民力大困。

translations.literal: When commoners sued over fields, even if there were not a dozen households, Zhang invariably ordered the whole prefecture to re-survey, hoping to broaden the registered acreage and increase state levies; within only a few years the people's strength was greatly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: When peasants sued over land, even if fewer than a dozen households were involved, Zhang ordered a full prefectural resurvey, hoping to expand the tax rolls and increase state revenue; within a few years the people were exhausted.

sentences.zh: 章與楊邠不喜儒士，郡官所請月俸，皆取不堪資軍者給之，謂之「閑雜物」，命所司高估其價，估定更添，謂之「擡估」，章亦不滿其意，隨事更令更添估。

translations.literal: Zhang and Yang Bin did not like Confucian scholars; the monthly salaries requested by prefectural officials were all paid in goods unfit for supplying the army, called "miscellaneous idle goods"; he ordered the responsible offices to overvalue their prices, and after valuation to add more, called "mark-up valuation"; Zhang was still not satisfied and ordered further mark-ups case by case.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang and Yang Bin disliked scholars; prefectural officials' monthly salaries were paid in goods unfit for military use, called "miscellaneous goods." The responsible offices were ordered to overvalue them, then mark them up again—called "inflated valuation"—and Zhang was still not satisfied and ordered further mark-ups on every occasion.

sentences.zh: 章急於財賦，峻於刑法，民有犯鹽礬酒曲之令，雖絲毫滴瀝，盡處極刑。

translations.literal: Zhang was urgent about taxes and levies and severe in penal law; if commoners violated regulations on salt, alum, wine, or yeast, even the slightest drop received the extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang was frantic about revenue and harsh in law; violations of salt, alum, wine, or yeast monopolies, however slight, brought the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 吏緣為奸，民不堪命。

translations.literal: Clerks took advantage to practice villainy, and the people could not bear their fate.
translations.idiomatic: Officials used the laws to practice every kind of extortion, and the people could not endure it.

sentences.zh: 章與楊邠同郡，尤為親愛，其獎用進拔者，莫非鄉舊。

translations.literal: Zhang and Yang Bin were from the same commandery and were especially close; those he rewarded, employed, and promoted were none but hometown associates.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang and Yang Bin were from the same commandery and were especially close; everyone Zhang promoted was a fellow townsman.

sentences.zh: 常輕視文臣，曰：「此等若與一把算子，未知顛倒，何益於事！

translations.literal: He often looked down on civil officials and said: "If you gave these fellows an abacus, they would not know which way to turn it—what good are they for affairs!
translations.idiomatic: He often despised civil officials and said, "Give these fellows an abacus and they would not know which end is up—what use are they?

sentences.zh: 」後因私第開宴席，召賓客，史宏肇、蘇逢吉乘醉喧詬而罷。

translations.literal: " Later, because he held a banquet at his private residence and summoned guests, Shi Hongzhao and Su Fengji, drunk, shouted abuse and the gathering broke up.
translations.idiomatic: " Later he gave a banquet at his home; Shi Hongzhao and Su Fengji, drunk, shouted abuse and the party broke up in disorder.

sentences.zh: 章自是忽忽不樂，潛求外任。

translations.literal: From this Zhang was listless and unhappy and secretly sought an outside appointment.
translations.idiomatic: After this Zhang grew depressed and secretly sought a post outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 邠與宏肇深沮其意。

translations.literal: Bin and Hongzhao deeply obstructed his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Bin and Hongzhao firmly blocked his wish.

sentences.zh: 而私第數有怪異，章愈懷憂恐。

translations.literal: Yet his private residence repeatedly had strange omens, and Zhang grew ever more anxious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Strange omens appeared repeatedly at his house, and Zhang grew ever more fearful.

sentences.zh: 乾祐三年冬，與史宏肇、楊邠等遇害，夷其族。

translations.literal: In winter of the third year of Qianyou, together with Shi Hongzhao, Yang Bin, and others he met with disaster and his clan was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of the third year of Qianyou he was killed along with Shi Hongzhao, Yang Bin, and the others, and his clan was exterminated.

sentences.zh: 妻白氏，禍前數月而卒。

translations.literal: His wife, the Bai clan, had died several months before the disaster.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, née Bai, had died several months before the massacre.

sentences.zh: 無子，惟一女，適戶部員外郎張貽肅，羸疾逾年，扶病就戮。

translations.literal: He had no sons, only one daughter, married to Zhang Yisu, an outer official of the Ministry of Revenue; ill and wasted for more than a year, she was led to execution while supporting herself in sickness.
translations.idiomatic: He had no sons, only a daughter married to Zhang Yisu of the Ministry of Revenue; ill for more than a year, she was dragged to execution while barely able to stand.

sentences.zh: 閻晉卿者，忻州人也。

translations.literal: Yan Jinqing was a native of Xinzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jinqing came from Xinzhou.

sentences.zh: 家世富豪，少仕並門，歷職至客將，高祖在鎮，頗見信用。

translations.literal: His family had been wealthy for generations; in youth he served at Bing Gate, rose through posts to guest general, and when Gaozu was in his governorship was greatly trusted.
translations.idiomatic: His family had been wealthy for generations. He entered service young at Taiyuan, rose to guest general, and won Emperor Gaozu's trust when Gaozu governed there.

sentences.zh: 乾祐中，歷閣門使，判四方館。

translations.literal: During Qianyou he served as gate commissioner and concurrently directed the Four Quarters Office.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianyou he served as gate commissioner and director of the Four Quarters Office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，關西亂，郭從義討趙思綰於京兆，晉卿偏師以攻賊壘。

translations.literal: Before long Guanxi was in disorder; Guo Congyi campaigned against Zhao Sijian at Jingzhao, and Jinqing led a detached force to attack the rebel fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Guanxi rebelled; Guo Congyi campaigned against Zhao Sijian at Jingzhao, and Jinqing led a detached force against the rebel camps.

sentences.zh: （《宋史·李韜傳》：周祖征三叛，韜從白文珂攻河中，兵傅其城。

translations.literal: (From the Biography of Li Tao in the 《History of Song》: The Zhou ancestor campaigned against the three rebellions; Tao followed Bai Wenke in attacking Hezhong, and the army pressed against its walls.
translations.idiomatic: (From the Biography of Li Tao in the 《History of Song》: When the Zhou founder campaigned against the three rebellions, Tao followed Bai Wenke in attacking Hezhong and pressed the army against its walls.

sentences.zh: 文珂夜詣周祖議犒軍，留韜城下。

translations.literal: Wenke by night went to the Zhou ancestor to discuss rewarding the army and left Tao below the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wenke went by night to discuss army rewards with the Zhou founder and left Tao below the walls.

sentences.zh: 時營柵未備，李守貞乘虛來襲，營中忽見火發，知賊驟至，惶怖失據。

translations.literal: At the time the camp palisade was not yet complete; Li Shouzhen seized the opportunity to attack; fire suddenly broke out in the camp; they knew the rebels had come swiftly and were terrified and at a loss.
translations.idiomatic: The camp palisade was not yet finished when Li Shouzhen attacked by surprise; fire broke out in the camp, the men knew the enemy was upon them, and panic seized them.

sentences.zh: 客省使閻晉卿率左右數十人，遇韜於月城側，謂韜曰：「事急矣。

translations.literal: The guest-reception commissioner Yan Jinqing led several tens of his attendants, met Tao beside the moon wall, and said to Tao: "The matter is urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Guest-reception Commissioner Yan Jinqing led several dozen men, met Tao by the moon wall, and said, "This is urgent.

sentences.zh: 城中人悉被黃紙甲，為火光所照，色俱白，此殊易辨，奈軍士無鬥志何！

translations.literal: All in the city wear yellow-paper armor; illuminated by the firelight they all appear white—this is very easy to distinguish, but what can be done when the soldiers have no fighting spirit!
translations.idiomatic: Everyone in the city wears yellow-paper armor; in the firelight it all looks white and is easy to tell apart—but what can we do when the soldiers have no will to fight!

sentences.zh: 」韜憤怒曰：「豈有食君祿而不為國致死耶！

translations.literal: " Tao said angrily: "How can one eat the ruler's salary and not die for the state!
translations.idiomatic: " Tao said angrily, "How can men who eat the ruler's grain refuse to die for the state!

sentences.zh: 」即援槊而進，軍中死士十餘輩，隨韜犯賊鋒。

translations.literal: " He immediately took up his spear and advanced; more than ten death-defying soldiers in the army followed Tao and struck the rebel front.
translations.idiomatic: " He seized his spear and charged forward; a dozen die-hard soldiers followed him into the enemy line.

sentences.zh: 蒲有猛將，躍馬持戈擬韜，韜刺之，洞胸而墜，又連殺數十人，蒲軍遂潰，因擊大破之。）〉

translations.literal: Hezhong had a fierce general who leaped on his horse and aimed his halberd at Tao; Tao stabbed him, pierced his chest, and he fell; he then killed several tens more in succession; the Hezhong army broke and was thereupon struck and greatly defeated.))〉
translations.idiomatic: A fierce Hezhong general spurred his horse and leveled his halberd at Tao; Tao ran him through the chest and he fell; Tao killed several dozen more in succession, the Hezhong army broke, and the attackers won a great victory.))〉

sentences.zh: 賊平，為內客省使，丁父憂，起復前職。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified he became commissioner of the inner service; on his father's death he mourned, then was recalled to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were defeated he was made commissioner of the inner service; when his father died he mourned, then was recalled to his former post.

sentences.zh: 時宣徽使闕，晉卿以職次事望，合當其任，既而久稽拜命，晉卿頗怨執政。

translations.literal: At the time the post of palace secretariat commissioner was vacant; Jinqing by seniority and expectation of office ought to have received it, yet the appointment was long delayed, and Jinqing resented those in power.
translations.idiomatic: The post of palace secretariat commissioner was vacant; by seniority Jinqing expected it, but the appointment was long delayed and he resented the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 會李業等謀殺楊、史，詔晉卿謀之。

translations.literal: It happened that Li Ye and others plotted to kill Yang and Shi; the emperor ordered Jinqing to join the plot.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Ye and others plotted to kill Yang Bin and Shi Hongzhao, the emperor ordered Jinqing to take part.

sentences.zh: 晉卿退詣宏肇，將告其事，宏肇不見。

translations.literal: Jinqing withdrew and went to Hongzhao intending to inform him of the matter; Hongzhao would not see him.
translations.idiomatic: Jinqing withdrew and went to warn Hongzhao, but Hongzhao refused to see him.

sentences.zh: 晉卿憂事不果，夜懸高祖御容於中堂，泣禱於前，遲明戎服入朝。

translations.literal: Jinqing feared the affair would not succeed; at night he hung Gaozu's imperial portrait in the central hall and wept in prayer before it; at dawn he entered court in military dress.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the plot would succeed, Jinqing hung Emperor Gaozu's portrait in his hall that night and wept before it in prayer; at dawn he entered court in armor.

sentences.zh: 內難既作，以晉卿權侍衛馬軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: Once the inner crisis had begun, Jinqing was made acting commander of the palace guard cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When the palace coup began, Jinqing was made acting commander of the palace guard cavalry.

sentences.zh: 北郊兵敗，晉卿乃自殺於家。

translations.literal: When the army was defeated at the northern suburb, Jinqing then killed himself at home.
translations.idiomatic: When the army was defeated at the northern suburb, Jinqing killed himself at home.

sentences.zh: 聶文進，并州人。

translations.literal: Nie Wenjin was a man of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Nie Wenjin was from Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 少給事於高祖帳下，高祖鎮太原，甚見委用，職至兵馬押司官。

translations.literal: In youth he served in Gaozu's tent; when Gaozu governed Taiyuan he was greatly entrusted and rose to the post of horse-and-army custody clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he served in Emperor Gaozu's household; when Gaozu governed Taiyuan he was greatly trusted and rose to horse-and-army custody clerk.

sentences.zh: 高祖入汴，授樞密院承旨，歷領軍、屯衛大將軍，遷右衛大將軍，仍領舊職。

translations.literal: When Gaozu entered Bian he was appointed director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, successively held the posts of general of the army and general of the garrison guard, was transferred to general of the right guard, and still held his former post.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu entered Bian he was made director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, served as army general and garrison guard general, was promoted to right guard general, and retained his former duties.

sentences.zh: 遇周太祖出征，稍至驕橫，久未遷改，深所怨望，與李業輩構成變亂。

translations.literal: When the Zhou ancestor went on campaign he gradually became arrogant and overbearing; long without promotion, he deeply resented it and with Li Ye and his kind brought about the mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Wei went on campaign Wenjin grew arrogant; long without promotion, he nursed a deep grievance and with Li Ye and others engineered the coup.

sentences.zh: 史宏肇等遇害之前夕，文進與同黨預作宣詔，制置朝廷之事，凡關文字，並出文進之手。

translations.literal: On the eve of Shi Hongzhao and the others meeting disaster, Wenjin and his confederates prepared proclamations in advance, arranged court affairs, and all documents issued from Wenjin's hand.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of Shi Hongzhao's murder, Wenjin and his allies drafted proclamations in advance and arranged court affairs; every document came from Wenjin's hand.

sentences.zh: 明日難作，文進點閱兵籍，征發軍眾，指揮取舍，以為己任，內外咨稟，前後填咽。

translations.literal: The next day when the crisis broke out, Wenjin inspected the military registers, mobilized troops, and directed acceptance and rejection as his own responsibility; consultations inside and outside were jammed before and behind.
translations.idiomatic: The next day, when the coup broke out, Wenjin inspected the rolls, mobilized troops, and directed everything himself; the court was overwhelmed with his orders.

sentences.zh: 太祖在鄴被構，初謂文進不預其事，驗其事跡，方知文進亂階之首也，大詬詈之。

translations.literal: The ancestor at Ye was framed; at first he thought Wenjin was not involved in the affair; verifying the facts, he then knew Wenjin was the chief of those who raised disorder and reviled him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Wei at Ye was framed, he first thought Wenjin was innocent; when he verified the facts he learned Wenjin had been the chief instigator and cursed him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 太祖過封丘，帝次於北郊，文進告太后曰：「臣在此，請宮中勿憂。

translations.literal: When the ancestor passed Fengqiu, the emperor halted at the northern suburb; Wenjin told the empress dowager: "Your servant is here—please do not worry within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: As Guo Wei passed Fengqiu, the emperor camped at the northern suburb; Wenjin told the empress dowager, "I am here—there is no need for alarm within the palace.

sentences.zh: 」兵散之後，文進召同黨痛飲，歌笑自若。

translations.literal: " After the army dispersed, Wenjin summoned his confederates to drink heavily, singing and laughing as if at ease.
translations.idiomatic: " After the army broke up, Wenjin summoned his allies for a drunken feast, singing and laughing as if nothing had happened.

sentences.zh: 遲明，帝遇禍，文進奔竄，為軍士所追，梟其首。

translations.literal: At dawn the emperor met with disaster; Wenjin fled in panic, was pursued by soldiers, and his head was displayed.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the emperor was killed; Wenjin fled, was pursued by soldiers, and his head was displayed.

sentences.zh: 後贊，為飛龍使。

translations.literal: Hou Zan served as commissioner of the Flying Dragon guard.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Zan served as commissioner of the Flying Dragon guard.

sentences.zh: 贊母本倡家也，與父同郡，往來其家，生贊。

translations.literal: Zan's mother had originally been of an entertainer's household; he and Zan's father were from the same commandery and visited her home, and Zan was born.
translations.idiomatic: Zan's mother had been an entertainer; his father, from the same commandery, visited her house, and Zan was born.

sentences.zh: 從職四方，父未嘗離郡，贊既長，疑其所生。

translations.literal: Following office in all directions, the father had never left the commandery; when Zan grew up he doubted who had borne him.
translations.idiomatic: The father served in posts across the realm but never left their home commandery; when Zan grew up he doubted his parentage.

sentences.zh: 及為內職，不欲父之來，寓書以致其意。

translations.literal: When he held an inner-service post he did not want his father to come and sent a letter to convey his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held an inner-service post he did not want his father to visit and sent a letter to make this clear.

sentences.zh: 父自郡至京師，直抵其第，贊不得已而奉之。

translations.literal: The father came from the commandery to the capital, went straight to his residence, and Zan had no choice but to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: His father came from the commandery to the capital, went straight to his house, and Zan had no choice but to receive him.

sentences.zh: 乾祐末，宰相楊祐、侍衛親軍使史宏肇執權，贊以久次未遷，頗懷怨望，乃與樞密承旨聶文進等構變。

translations.literal: At the end of Qianyou, Chancellor Yang You and the commander of the palace guard personal army Shi Hongzhao held power; Zan, long without promotion, harbored resentment and together with the military affairs director Nie Wenjin and others engineered the mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Qianyou, Chancellor Yang Bin and Palace Guard Commander Shi Hongzhao held power; Zan, long passed over for promotion, nursed a grievance and joined Military Affairs Director Nie Wenjin and others in plotting the coup.

sentences.zh: 及難作，贊與同黨更侍帝側，剖判戎事，且防間言。

translations.literal: When the crisis broke out, Zan and his confederates in turn attended at the emperor's side, decided military affairs, and also guarded against slander.
translations.idiomatic: When the coup broke out, Zan and his allies attended the emperor in shifts, directed military affairs, and guarded against rumors.

sentences.zh: 北郊兵敗，贊竄歸兗州，慕容彥超執之以獻，有司鞫贊伏罪，周太祖命誅之。

translations.literal: When the army was defeated at the northern suburb, Zan fled to Yanzhou; Murong Yanchao seized him and presented him; the responsible offices interrogated him until he confessed guilt; the Zhou ancestor ordered his execution.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at the northern suburb, Zan fled to Yanzhou; Murong Yanchao seized him and handed him over; the courts tried him until he confessed, and Emperor Taizu of Zhou ordered his execution.

sentences.zh: 郭允明者，小名竇十，河東人也。

translations.literal: Guo Yuming, whose childhood name was Dou Ten, was a man of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yuming, nicknamed Dou Ten, was from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 幼隸河東制置使範徽柔，被誅，允明遂為高祖廝養，服勤既久，頗得高祖之歡心。

translations.literal: In youth he was a servant under Fan Huirou, military commissioner of Hedong; when Huirou was executed, Yuming became Gaozu's household servant; after long diligent service he won Gaozu's favor.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he served Military Commissioner Fan Huirou of Hedong; when Fan was executed, Yuming became Emperor Gaozu's household servant, and after long loyal service won the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 高祖鎮太原，稍歷牙職，及即位，累遷至翰林茶酒使兼鞍轡庫使。

translations.literal: When Gaozu governed Taiyuan he gradually held staff posts; when he took the throne Yuming rose through transfers to Hanlin tea-and-wine commissioner and concurrent commissioner of the saddle and bridle storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu governed Taiyuan he rose through staff posts; at his accession Yuming was promoted to Hanlin tea-and-wine commissioner and commissioner of the saddle and bridle storehouse.

sentences.zh: 隱帝嗣位，尤見親狎，每恃寵驕縱，略無禮敬。

translations.literal: When the Hidden Emperor succeeded he was especially intimate with him; relying on favor he was arrogant and unrestrained, with hardly any courtesy or respect.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yindi succeeded, Yuming became especially intimate with him; trusting in favor, he was arrogant and showed no respect.

sentences.zh: 與相州節度使郭謹以同宗之故，頗交結。

translations.literal: With Guo Jin, military governor of Xiangzhou, he was on rather close terms because of shared clan ties.
translations.idiomatic: He was on close terms with Guo Jin, military governor of Xiangzhou, because they shared a clan name.

sentences.zh: 謹在鎮，允明常賫禦酒以遺之，不以僭上犯禁為意。

translations.literal: While Jin was in his governorship, Yuming often sent imperial wine as gifts to him, without regard for the offense of overstepping authority and violating prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: While Jin governed his region, Yuming often sent him imperial wine as gifts without a thought for the crime of misusing the emperor's property.

sentences.zh: 其他輕率，悉皆類此，執政大臣頗姑息之。

translations.literal: His other rash acts were all of this kind, and the chief ministers in power largely indulged him.
translations.idiomatic: His other reckless acts were all of this sort, and the chief ministers largely indulged him.

sentences.zh: 嘗奉使荊南，車服導從，有同節度使將，州縣郵驛，奔馳畏懾，節度使高保融承迎不暇。

translations.literal: Once on a mission to Jingnan, his carriage, robes, and escort were like those of a military governor on campaign; prefectures, districts, and postal stations raced in fear; Military Governor Gao Baorong could scarcely keep up with receiving him.
translations.idiomatic: Once on a mission to Jingnan his carriage, dress, and escort rivaled a military governor's; prefectures and postal stations scrambled in fear, and Military Governor Gao Baorong could barely keep pace with his receptions.

sentences.zh: 允明潛使人步度城壁之高庳、池隍之廣隘，以動荊人，冀得重賄。

translations.literal: Yuming secretly sent men to pace and measure the height and low points of the walls and the breadth and narrowness of the moats, to intimidate the people of Jing, hoping to obtain heavy bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Yuming secretly sent men to measure the height of the walls and the breadth of the moats to intimidate the people of Jingnan, hoping for heavy bribes.

sentences.zh: 乾祐末，兼飛龍使。

translations.literal: At the end of Qianyou he held the Flying Dragon commission concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Qianyou he was also made commissioner of the Flying Dragon guard.

sentences.zh: 未幾，與李業輩構變，楊邠等諸子，允明親刃之於朝堂西廡下。

translations.literal: Before long, together with Li Ye and his kind he engineered the mutiny; Yang Bin and the others—Yuming personally ran them through with his blade under the western veranda of the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he joined Li Ye and others in the coup; Yang Bin and his colleagues Yuming killed with his own hand under the western veranda of the court hall.

sentences.zh: 王章女婿戶部員外郎張貽肅，血流逆註，聞者哀之。

translations.literal: Wang Zhang's son-in-law Zhang Yisu, outer official of the Ministry of Revenue, had blood flowing backward—those who heard of it pitied him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhang's son-in-law Zhang Yisu of the Ministry of Revenue bled so profusely that blood seemed to flow backward; all who heard of it were moved to pity.

sentences.zh: 及北郊之敗，允明迫帝就民舍，手行弒逆，尋亦自殺。

translations.literal: When the northern suburb was defeated, Yuming forced the emperor into a commoner's house and personally carried out regicide; soon after he also killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat at the northern suburb, Yuming forced the emperor into a commoner's house and murdered him with his own hand; soon afterward he killed himself as well.

sentences.zh: 劉銖，陜州人也。

translations.literal: Liu Zhu was a native of Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhu came from Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 少事梁邵王朱友誨為牙將。

translations.literal: In youth he served Prince Shao of Liang, Zhu Youhui, as a staff general.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he served Prince Shao of Liang, Zhu Youhui, as a staff general.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，高祖為侍衛親軍都指揮使，與銖有舊，乃表為內職。

translations.literal: During Tianfu in Jin, Gaozu was commander of the palace guard personal army; he had old ties with Zhu and memorialized him for an inner-service post.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianfu reign of Jin, when Emperor Gaozu was commander of the palace guard, he and Zhu were old acquaintances, and Gaozu recommended him for an inner-service post.

sentences.zh: 高祖出鎮並門，用為左都押牙。

translations.literal: When Gaozu went out to govern Bing Gate, Zhu was employed as left chief military adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was posted to govern Taiyuan, Zhu was made his left chief military adjutant.

sentences.zh: 銖性慘毒好殺，高祖以為勇斷類己，深委遇之。

translations.literal: Zhu's nature was cruel, poisonous, and fond of killing; Gaozu thought him brave and decisive like himself and deeply entrusted and favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu was cruel and bloodthirsty by nature; Gaozu thought him bold and resolute like himself and relied on him deeply.

sentences.zh: 國初，授永興軍節度使，從定汴、洛、移鎮青州，加同平章事。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state he was appointed military governor of Yongxing Army; he followed in pacifying Bian and Luo, was transferred to govern Qingzhou, and was made Tongpingzhangshi.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynasty's founding he was made military governor of Yongxing; he helped pacify Bian and Luoyang, was transferred to Qingzhou, and made Tongpingzhangshi.

sentences.zh: 隱帝即位，加檢校太師、兼侍中。

translations.literal: When the Hidden Emperor succeeded, Zhu was given the additional titles of honorary grand preceptor and concurrent palace secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yindi came to the throne, Zhu was made honorary grand preceptor and concurrent palace secretary.

sentences.zh: 銖立法深峻，令行禁止，吏民有過，不問輕重，未嘗貸免。

translations.literal: Zhu made laws deep and severe; orders were enforced and prohibitions observed; if officials or commoners had offenses, without asking light or heavy, he never granted exemption.
