translations.idiomatic: Zhu's laws were harsh and strictly enforced; officials and commoners alike who offended, whether gravely or slightly, were never spared.

sentences.zh: 每親事，小有忤旨，即令倒曳而出，至數百步外方止，膚體無完者。

translations.literal: Whenever he personally handled affairs, if there was the slightest offense against his intent, he would order the person dragged out head downward until several hundred paces away before stopping; not a patch of skin remained whole.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he handled a case in person, the slightest offense would bring an order to drag the offender head-down for hundreds of paces; not an inch of skin was left whole.

sentences.zh: 每杖人，遣雙杖對下，謂之「合歡杖」；

translations.literal: Whenever he flogged someone, he sent paired clubs down together, calling it the "joyous union club";
translations.idiomatic: When he flogged someone, he had two clubs strike together, calling it the "joyous union flogging";

sentences.zh: 或杖人如其歲數，謂之「隨年杖」。

translations.literal: or he flogged a person according to his years of age, calling it the "age-matching club."
translations.idiomatic: or he flogged a man once for each year of his age, calling it the "age-matching flogging."

sentences.zh: 在任擅行賦斂，每秋苗一畝率錢三千，夏苗一畝錢二千，以備公用，部內畏之，脅肩重跡。

translations.literal: While in office he levied taxes at will; each autumn field acre averaged three thousand cash, each summer field acre two thousand, to supply public use; within his jurisdiction they feared him, shrugging shoulders and walking with heavy steps.
translations.idiomatic: In office he levied taxes at will—three thousand cash per acre of autumn crop and two thousand per acre of summer crop for public expenses. His domain feared him; men walked with hunched shoulders and heavy tread.

sentences.zh: 乾祐中，淄、青大蝗，銖下令捕蝗，略無遺漏，田苗無害。

translations.literal: During Qianyou there was a great locust plague in Zi and Qing; Zhu ordered locusts captured, with hardly any missed, and the field crops were unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: During Qianyou a great locust plague struck Zi and Qing; Zhu ordered a locust hunt so thorough that scarcely one escaped, and the crops were saved.

sentences.zh: 先是，濱海郡邑，皆有兩浙回易務，厚取民利，自置刑禁，追攝王民，前後長吏利其厚賂，不能禁止。

translations.literal: Earlier, in coastal commanderies and districts there were exchange offices of the Two Zhe, which heavily took profit from the people, set up their own punishments and prohibitions, and pursued and seized the ruler's subjects; successive chief officials profited from their heavy bribes and could not forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal districts had long housed exchange offices of the Two Zhe, which extorted the people, enforced their own punishments, and seized imperial subjects at will; successive governors took their heavy bribes and could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 銖即告所部，不得與吳越征負，擅行追攝，浙人惕息，莫敢幹命。

translations.literal: Zhu immediately announced to his jurisdiction that they must not collect debts for Wu and Yue or pursue and seize on their own; the people of Zhe drew in their breath in fear and none dared defy his orders.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu at once forbade his jurisdiction to collect debts for Wu and Yue or to pursue people on their behalf; the Zhe merchants held their breath in fear and none dared defy him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷懼銖之剛戾難制，因前浙州刺史郭瓊自海州用兵還，過青州，遂留之，即以府彥卿代銖，銖即時受代。

translations.literal: The court feared Zhu's stubborn violence was hard to control; because the former prefect of Zhe Guo Qiong was returning from campaigning at Haizhou and passed through Qingzhou, he was kept there and Fu Yanqing was sent to replace Zhu; Zhu immediately accepted the transfer.
translations.idiomatic: The court feared Zhu's brutal obstinacy; when former Zhe Prefect Guo Qiong returned from campaigning at Haizhou and passed through Qingzhou, he was kept there and Fu Yanqing replaced Zhu, who accepted the transfer at once.

sentences.zh: （《隆平集》《郭瓊傳》云：劉銖守平盧，稱疾不朝，隱帝疑其叛，詔瓊領兵屯青州。

translations.literal: (The 《Longping Collection》, Biography of Guo Qiong, says: Liu Zhu guarded Pinglu, claimed illness and did not come to court; the Hidden Emperor suspected rebellion and ordered Qiong to lead troops and encamp at Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Longping Collection》, Biography of Guo Qiong, says: Liu Zhu held Pinglu, claimed illness, and refused to come to court; Emperor Yindi suspected rebellion and ordered Qiong to encamp at Qingzhou with troops.

sentences.zh: 銖將害之，張宴伏兵幕下，瓊無懼色，銖亦不敢發。

translations.literal: Zhu intended to harm him and spread a banquet with ambush troops beneath the tent; Qiong showed no fear, and Zhu also did not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu planned to kill him and set an ambush beneath the banquet tent, but Qiong showed no fear, and Zhu did not dare strike.

sentences.zh: 瓊為言去就禍福，銖趨召。）〉

translations.literal: Qiong spoke to him of the fortune and misfortune of staying or going; Zhu hurried to answer the summons.))〉
translations.idiomatic: Qiong spoke to him of the consequences of staying or leaving, and Zhu hurried to obey the summons.))〉

sentences.zh: 離鎮之日，有私鹽數屋，雜以糞穢，填塞諸井，以土平之。

translations.literal: On the day he left his governorship there were several rooms of private salt mixed with filth; he filled all the wells and leveled them with earth.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he left his post he had several rooms of illicit salt mixed with filth, filled every well with it, and covered them with earth.

sentences.zh: 彥卿發其事以聞，銖奉朝請久之，每潛戟手於史宏肇、楊邠第。

translations.literal: Yanqing exposed the matter and reported it; Zhu attended court for a long time as a court gentleman, and each time secretly clenched his fists outside the residences of Shi Hongzhao and Yang Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqing exposed the affair and reported it; Zhu attended court for a long time as a court gentleman and would secretly clench his fists outside the homes of Shi Hongzhao and Yang Bin.

sentences.zh: 會李業輩同誅宏肇等，銖喜，謂業輩曰：「君等可謂僂羅兒矣。

translations.literal: It happened that Li Ye and his kind together executed Hongzhao and the others; Zhu was pleased and said to Ye and his kind: "You can indeed be called louluo'er.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Ye and his allies killed Hongzhao and the others, Zhu rejoiced and told them, "You fellows have shown yourselves true hard men.

sentences.zh: 」尋以銖權知開封府事，周太祖親族及王峻家，並為銖所害。

translations.literal: " Soon Zhu was made acting administrator of Kaifeng prefecture; the Zhou ancestor's kin and Wang Jun's household were all harmed by Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon Zhu was made acting prefect of Kaifeng; he murdered the kin of Guo Wei and the household of Wang Jun.

sentences.zh: 周太祖入京城，執之下獄。

translations.literal: When the Zhou ancestor entered the capital, Zhu was seized and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Wei entered the capital, Zhu was arrested and thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 銖謂妻曰：「我則死矣，君應與人為婢耳！

translations.literal: Zhu said to his wife: "I shall die; you will have to become someone's maidservant!
translations.idiomatic: Zhu told his wife, "I am as good as dead—you will have to become someone's servant girl!

sentences.zh: 」妻曰：「明公所為如是，雅合為之。

translations.literal: " His wife said: "What my lord has done is such that it is only fitting.
translations.idiomatic: " His wife replied, "Given what you have done, my lord, it is only fitting.

sentences.zh: 」周太祖遣人讓銖曰：「昔日與公常同事漢室，寧無故人之情，家屬屠滅，公雖奉君命，加之酷毒，一何忍哉！

translations.literal: " The Zhou ancestor sent someone to reproach Zhu: "In former days I often served the Han house together with you—was there no feeling of old friendship? Your slaughter of my household—though you followed the ruler's command, to add such cruelty—how could you be so ruthless!
translations.idiomatic: " Guo Wei sent a man to rebuke Zhu: "We once served the Han house together—was there no bond of old friendship? You slaughtered my family; though you followed the emperor's order, to add such cruelty—how could you be so ruthless!

sentences.zh: 公家亦有妻子，還顧念否？

translations.literal: Your household too has wife and children—do you not look back and consider?
translations.idiomatic: You have a wife and children of your own—have you no thought for them?

sentences.zh: 」銖但稱死罪。

translations.literal: " Zhu could only plead guilty unto death.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhu could only plead guilty and await death.

sentences.zh: 遂啟太后，並一子誅之，而釋其妻。

translations.literal: He then reported to the empress dowager and executed Zhu together with one son, but released his wife.
translations.idiomatic: He then reported to the empress dowager, executed Zhu and one son, but released his wife.

sentences.zh: 周太祖踐阼，詔賜銖妻陜州莊宅各一區。

translations.literal: When the Zhou ancestor took the throne, he decreed gifts to Zhu's wife of one estate and one residence each in Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizu of Zhou took the throne, he decreed that Zhu's wife be given an estate and a residence in Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: （《五代史闕文》：漢隱帝朝，銖為開封尹，周祖自鄴起兵，銖盡誅周祖之家子孫婦女十數人，極其慘毒。

translations.literal: (The 《Supplementary Texts to the History of the Five Dynasties》: During the Hidden Emperor's Han, Zhu was prefect of Kaifeng; the Zhou ancestor raised troops from Ye; Zhu executed all of the Zhou ancestor's household—more than ten men, women, and children—with extreme cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Supplementary Texts to the History of the Five Dynasties》: During Emperor Yindi's reign Zhu was prefect of Kaifeng; when the Zhou founder raised troops from Ye, Zhu slaughtered more than a dozen of Guo Wei's kin, men and women alike, with extreme cruelty.

sentences.zh: 及隱帝遇害，周祖以漢太后令，收銖下獄，使人責之。

translations.literal: When the Hidden Emperor met with disaster, the Zhou ancestor by the Han empress dowager's order seized Zhu and imprisoned him, and sent someone to reproach him.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yindi was killed, Guo Wei, by order of the Han empress dowager, arrested Zhu and sent a man to rebuke him.

sentences.zh: 銖對曰：「某為漢家戮叛族耳，不知其他。

translations.literal: Zhu replied: "I merely executed the rebel clan for the house of Han—I know nothing else.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu replied, "I merely executed a rebel clan for the house of Han—I know nothing beyond that.

sentences.zh: 」周祖怒，遂殺之。）〉

translations.literal: " The Zhou ancestor in anger then killed him.))〉
translations.idiomatic: " Guo Wei in anger had him killed.))〉

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：臣觀漢之亡也，豈系於天命哉！

translations.literal: The historian says: This subject observes that the fall of Han—was it bound to fate and heaven!
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: In my view, was the fall of Han really a matter of Heaven's mandate?

sentences.zh: 蓋委用不得其人，聽斷不符於理故也。

translations.literal: It was rather that the men entrusted and employed were not the right ones, and judgments did not accord with reason.
translations.idiomatic: Rather, the wrong men were put in power, and decisions no longer accorded with reason.

sentences.zh: 且如宏肇之淫刑，楊邠之秕政，李業、晉卿之設計，文進、允明之狂且，雖使成王為君，周公作相，亦不能保宗社之安，延歲月之命，況隱帝、逢吉之徒，其能免乎！

translations.literal: Consider Hongzhao's excessive punishments, Yang Bin's chaff policies, Li Ye and Jinqing's plotting, Wenjin and Yuming's madness and arrogance—even if King Cheng were ruler and the Duke of Zhou chancellor, they could not preserve the security of the ancestral temple or extend the mandate of years—how much less could the Hidden Emperor, Fengji, and their kind escape!
translations.idiomatic: Consider Hongzhao's savage punishments, Yang Bin's worthless governance, the plots of Li Ye and Jinqing, the reckless arrogance of Wenjin and Yuming—even with King Cheng on the throne and the Duke of Zhou as chancellor, the dynasty could not have been saved; how then could Emperor Yindi, Fengji, and men like them have escaped ruin!

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「大君有命，開國承家，小人勿用，必亂邦也。

translations.literal: The 《Changes》 says: "The great ruler has a mandate; he founds states and inherits families—petty men must not be employed, for they will surely disorder the state."
translations.idiomatic: The 《Book of Changes》 says: "The great ruler has a mandate to found states and establish families—petty men must not be employed, for they will surely bring the state to ruin."

sentences.zh: 」當乾祐之末也，何斯言之驗歟！

translations.literal: " At the end of Qianyou, how this saying was fulfilled!
translations.idiomatic: " At the end of Qianyou, how fully those words were fulfilled!

sentences.zh: 惟劉銖之忍酷，又安能逭於一死乎！

translations.literal: As for Liu Zhu's cruel brutality, how could he escape a single death!
translations.idiomatic: As for Liu Zhu's cruelty, how could he have escaped death?
